summary: Vela grounds transcendental facts in a necessary personal mind; Dillahunty argues that the inference remains underspecified, comparatively unsupported, and evidentially nondiscriminating.

pro.text: I'm asking the the meta question
pro.context: Vela distinguishes agreement about the reliable operation of transcendental facts from his further metaphysical question about what grounds them.

con.text: does this reliably point to the proposition that a god is the explanation
con.context: Dillahunty frames good evidence as support that discriminates reliably in favor of a sufficiently specific divine explanation.

pro-personal-mind-from-logical-attribute.words: Logical laws possess objective, necessary, timeless, immaterial, and transcendent attributes that are better explained by a transcendent personal mind than by naturalism or Platonism.
pro-personal-mind-from-logical-attribute.critique: Strongest feature: The move directly supplies the indispensable personal-ground bridge by connecting an identifiable cluster of logical attributes with the proposed transcendent mind, giving the constructive case a clear destination and substantial relevance. Principal limitation: Its elimination language compresses several controversial transitions, treating difficulties for naturalism and Platonism as though agency remains, while neither exhausting impersonal alternatives nor explaining why abstract necessity, timelessness, or causal inertness indicates personality. Live burden: The case still must distinguish grounding from explanation, show why truths must reside in a mind, and compare the strongest noncausal Platonist or fundamentalist accounts rather than merely declaring their failure. Locked score: The mixed band reflects excellent burden contact but materially overstated force, incomplete comparative warrant, partly unstable terminology, and an underdeveloped inference from logical attributes to an omnipotent personal ground.

pro-necessary-ground-not-brute-fact.words: Ignorance or brute-fact appeals do not remove the explanatory demand, whereas God is proposed as a self-existing necessary reality rather than an unexplained contingent posit.
pro-necessary-ground-not-brute-fact.critique: Strongest feature: The move places the grounding demand squarely at the center of the debate and clearly distinguishes the proposed divine ground from an ordinary contingent posit, thereby establishing a recognizable constructive route. Principal limitation: Calling God self-existing and necessary does not independently establish why that description answers an explanatory request unavailable to logical facts themselves, while the terms brute fact, necessity, and self-existence remain insufficiently differentiated. Live burden: The argument must provide a principled reason that necessary logical relations cannot be fundamental, explain what additional work divine necessity performs, and avoid granting God an exemption solely through redescriptive terminology. Locked score: The mixed band records strong relevance and a recoverable thesis alongside materially overstated necessity, limited evidential warrant, incomplete engagement with necessary-brute alternatives, and a central explanatory asymmetry that remains unsupported.

tags.label: Special pleading
tags.context: The divine posit receives explanatory termination through necessity without a developed reason that equally necessary logical facts cannot terminate explanation.

pro-unified-divine-explanation.words: A single divine ground can unify transcendental and other facts through coherence, parsimony, explanatory power, explanatory scope, and comparatively low ad hocness.
pro-unified-divine-explanation.critique: Strongest feature: The move usefully shifts from bare compatibility to familiar explanatory virtues, presenting the divine hypothesis as a unified account with coherence, scope, power, and comparatively low ad hocness across multiple facts. Principal limitation: It declares God exemplary across this matrix without conducting the necessary side-by-side comparisons, and its expansion from transcendental facts to many features of reality enlarges the claim beyond the supplied support. Live burden: The proposal must measure ontological and explanatory costs, address whether a personal divine mind is itself complex, and compare concrete naturalist, Platonist, and fundamentalist candidates under consistent criteria. Locked score: The mixed band reflects a coherent and highly relevant comparative framework whose conclusion remains materially overstated because the asserted parsimony and superiority are announced rather than demonstrated against the strongest available rivals.

con-evidence-reliable-discrimination.words: Good evidence should reduce bias and reliably favor a sufficiently specific, testable God hypothesis through repeatability, independent verification, falsifiability, or causal relevance.
con-evidence-reliable-discrimination.critique: Strongest feature: The move articulates a disciplined evidentiary standard centered on reliable discrimination, specificity, independent confirmation, and bias reduction, while carefully describing repeatability and falsifiability as ideal features rather than exceptionless requirements. Principal limitation: It does not separately test each explanatory virtue invoked for the divine account, and some metaphysical evidence may remain rationally relevant despite lacking experimental repetition or direct causal isolation. Live burden: The standard must explain how philosophical and historical evidence can receive appropriate weight, identify which divine predictions are sufficiently specific, and show why the offered transcendental considerations fail comparatively rather than merely failing laboratory ideals. Locked score: The very strong band reflects precise qualification, excellent burden relevance, coherent hypothesis-sensitive reasoning, and charitable allowance for nonexperimental evidence, with only limited incompleteness in its application to every constructive claim.

con-abduction-incomplete-candidate-set.words: Abduction becomes unreliable when its candidate set is poorly bounded, because compatibility with observations does not establish that an extraordinary hypothesis is the likeliest explanation.
con-abduction-incomplete-candidate-set.critique: Strongest feature: The move directly challenges the comparative structure of the theistic abduction and memorably distinguishes reasonable ordinary inference from confidence in extraordinary candidates when the relevant possibility space, priors, and alternatives are poorly understood. Principal limitation: Its language about unreliability is broader than the supporting analogy warrants, because abduction can responsibly rank known explanations without possessing an exhaustive candidate list when background frequencies and comparative expectations are independently justified. Live burden: The objection must specify how incomplete the candidate set is, which omitted rivals are genuinely live, and why uncertainty about unknown possibilities materially weakens this particular divine comparison rather than every abductive inference. Locked score: The strong band reflects clear responsiveness, good calibration through the ordinary-case concession, and serious underdetermination pressure, moderated by an imprecise completeness threshold and no fully developed alternative account.

con-vague-divine-hypothesis.words: A generalized classical-theist mind or creator is too vague to function as a discrete hypothesis capable of being reliably favored by unexplained logic or order.
con-vague-divine-hypothesis.critique: Strongest feature: The reply identifies the crucial gap between attaching traditional attributes to a divine label and specifying a hypothesis whose expectations can be compared with rivals, directly pressuring the inference from logical facts to the motion's personal God. Principal limitation: It does not independently refute every property attributed to the proposed mind, and classical theism can offer substantive modal, personal, and maximal attributes even if their evidential implications require further articulation. Live burden: The objection should identify what operational or comparative content is missing, demonstrate how alternative divine or impersonal hypotheses predict the same data, and distinguish legitimate metaphysical abstraction from evidentially disabling vagueness. Locked score: The very strong band reflects precise terminology, proportionate force, direct burden contact, and a coherent discrimination challenge, with only a limited need for more property-specific rebuttal.

tags.label: Ambiguity effect
tags.context: The criticism materially concerns whether an underspecified divine hypothesis can be compared reliably rather than merely attracting confidence through familiar but vague attributes.

con-abduction-comparative-data-gap.words: A supernatural abduction lacks warrant without well-bounded candidates, comparative likelihood information, or confirmed divine causation, and cannot follow merely from missing natural explanations.
con-abduction-comparative-data-gap.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly attacks both negative elimination and comparative warrant, correctly observing that the absence of a presently accepted natural account does not by itself supply likelihood data favoring a divine cause. Principal limitation: Its demand for something approaching an exhaustive candidate set is insufficiently delimited, and the broader suggestion that good evidence for supernatural claims might be unavailable exceeds the narrower, better-supported criticism of this specific abduction. Live burden: The skeptical case must explain what comparative evidence would be sufficient, distinguish principled uncertainty from categorical exclusion, and identify serious candidate classes or prediction differences rather than resting entirely on missing data. Locked score: The strong band reflects substantial relevance, a persuasive warning against premature supernatural inference, and useful attention to causal baselines, tempered by overbroad framing and the absence of a complete positive rival.

con-hiddenness-evidential-expectation.words: Persistent obscurity and disagreement about unfalsifiable God claims conflict with the clarity reasonably expected if a capable classical-theist God wanted its existence widely known.
con-hiddenness-evidential-expectation.critique: Strongest feature: The move introduces an evidential expectation derived from divine capability and a possible desire for disclosure, offering issue-bearing contrary evidence against an uncomplicated personal-God hypothesis rather than merely denying the transcendental case. Principal limitation: It does not contact the decisive opening inference from logical attributes to a personal ground, and its suggestion that such a God would eliminate debate depends on underspecified assumptions about divine aims, human freedom, epistemic distance, and permissible ambiguity. Live burden: The hiddenness case must define the relevant disclosure intention, predict the expected distribution of reasonable nonbelief, and distinguish inadequate evidence from ordinary disagreement that could persist despite sufficient revelation. Locked score: The mixed band reflects genuine relevance to divine expectations but a nonanswer to the targeted grounding move, incomplete specification of the predicted evidence, and an overextended inference from disagreement alone.

con-logic-independent-of-god.words: Basic logical laws appear necessarily true whether or not God exists, and no personal or transcendent foundation has been demonstrated as necessary for their truth.
con-logic-independent-of-god.critique: Strongest feature: The reply squarely contests personal dependence by presenting identity and noncontradiction as apparently necessary across divine and nondivine possibilities, thereby contacting the central grounding claim rather than disputing logic's reality or usefulness. Principal limitation: Imaginability is an unstable guide to metaphysical possibility, and saying logical truths would remain true without God does not yet provide a developed truthmaker account or demonstrate that divine nature could not explain their necessity. Live burden: The position must clarify whether logic is fundamental, structural, conceptual, or descriptive and show why adding a personal ground offers no explanatory improvement rather than simply asserting independence. Locked score: The strong band reflects direct responsiveness, careful modal qualification, solid coherence, and meaningful pressure on divine dependence, while reserving room for a more rigorous account of necessity and explanation.

pro-abstract-truths-grounded-in-mind.words: Naturalism allegedly cannot ground transcendental facts, while abstract truths are intelligible as mental concepts and therefore fit more coherently within a transcendent mind.
pro-abstract-truths-grounded-in-mind.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly contacts the independence challenge by pairing an alleged failure of naturalistic grounding with a positive proposal that abstract truths are intelligible within mind, keeping attention on the contested personal-ground bridge. Principal limitation: Repeating that naturalism fails does not establish either that abstract truths are mental concepts or that a transcendent mind follows, and it risks sliding between human conceptual apprehension, propositions, truthmakers, and ontological grounds. Live burden: The argument must distinguish truths from thoughts about truths, explain how divine mentality secures objective necessity without making logic voluntary, and compare nonmental realist accounts on their strongest formulation. Locked score: The mixed band reflects direct relevance and a recoverable response, but the positive bridge remains compressed, the elimination is incomplete, and the evidential warrant does not match the asserted explanatory superiority.

tags.label: Equivocation
tags.context: The inference risks shifting between truths as abstract realities and concepts as objects of thought when moving from intelligibility to a mental ground.

con-logic-descriptive-no-further-ground.words: Logical and mathematical laws can describe identity and noncontradiction without requiring an additional entity or foundation to guarantee that their relations hold.
con-logic-descriptive-no-further-ground.critique: Strongest feature: The reply clearly separates the truth of logical or mathematical relations from any requirement for an additional guaranteeing entity, offering a direct and economical alternative to the initial grounding demand. Principal limitation: The arithmetic illustration establishes that a further ground is not obviously required in a simple case, but it does not demonstrate that every transcendental fact is merely descriptive or that all truthmaker and modal questions dissolve identically. Live burden: The position must explain why the demand for deeper explanation is illegitimate, clarify the ontological status of necessary relations, and show that adding a personal mind postpones rather than improves the account. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent precision, proportionate calibration, direct responsiveness, and a coherent challenge to explanatory addition, with a limited residual obligation to generalize beyond the illustration.

con-soundness-requires-supported-premise.words: A valid argument is not good evidence for God unless its premises are supported as true, because the disputed conclusion requires soundness rather than formal validity alone.
con-soundness-requires-supported-premise.critique: Strongest feature: The reply cleanly distinguishes validity from soundness and insists that a formally correct argument cannot establish the debated conclusion unless its substantive premises are adequately supported, directly reinforcing the central evidentiary burden. Principal limitation: It does not identify which particular premise fails or assess the offered abductive defenses individually, and actual soundness should be distinguished from the more accessible question of whether available evidence rationally supports premise truth. Live burden: The skeptical side must evaluate the grounding, personal-mind, and comparative premises separately and articulate what degree of support would make them reasonable without demanding certainty. Locked score: The very strong band reflects impeccable use of the core logical distinction, high relevance, matched force, and a decisive challenge to unsupported premises, moderated only by limited application to the argument's individual components.

pro-philosophical-abduction-as-evidence.words: Deductive implication and abductive premise support can constitute philosophical evidence, while restricting evidence to directly repeatable empirical observations would be self-undermining.
pro-philosophical-abduction-as-evidence.critique: Strongest feature: The reply correctly defends philosophical implication and abduction as legitimate forms of support, directly answering both the demand for warranted premises and any overly narrow interpretation of publicly repeatable evidence. Principal limitation: It treats logical positivism and an emphasis on direct empirical evidence as more interchangeable than the opposing formulation warrants, while calling the argument sound before independently establishing the disputed grounding and comparative premises. Live burden: The defense must move beyond admissibility and show that this particular abduction uses well-specified hypotheses, justified priors, and genuine comparative advantages over serious alternatives. Locked score: The strong band reflects high responsiveness, a coherent rejection of crude verificationism, and an important clarification of evidential categories, tempered by representational overreach and insufficient demonstration that the admitted method actually supports the proposed divine conclusion.

con-anomaly-does-not-identify-yahweh.words: Even an extraordinary celestial message could support generic agency without independently establishing Yahweh, necessity, personality, or another specific deity while rival explanations remain.
con-anomaly-does-not-identify-yahweh.critique: Strongest feature: The reply carefully grants that an extraordinary anomaly could count as evidence toward a god while distinguishing relevance, confirmation, sufficiency for conviction, and identification of Yahweh, thereby avoiding categorical evidential skepticism. Principal limitation: The move does not quantify how much the imagined event would favor generic agency or identify which additional observations would responsibly narrow the hypothesis, leaving its rival explanations largely schematic. Live burden: The skeptical case must state what bridging premises could move from anomalous agency to necessity, personality, or a specific deity and explain why the available transcendental evidence does not supply them. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional calibration, precise distinctions, direct responsiveness, and charitable acknowledgment of graded support, with only a modest need for a more developed comparative account of the remaining candidate explanations.

pro-unattainable-skeptical-link-standard.words: Requiring an incontrovertible link to God makes success unattainable if naturalistic, unknown, or brute-fact alternatives are always permitted regardless of the observation.
pro-unattainable-skeptical-link-standard.critique: Strongest feature: The move identifies a legitimate methodological danger: an evidentiary standard becomes unfairly insulated if every possible observation can be dismissed through an unspecified naturalistic, brute-fact, or unknown alternative without comparative assessment. Principal limitation: It shifts between reliable support, confirmation, and an incontrovertible link, overlooking the opponent's explicit concession that evidence may count toward God without uniquely identifying Yahweh or eliminating every residual possibility. Live burden: The reply must address the actual graded-discrimination standard, show where its threshold becomes excessive, and demonstrate that the pro evidence improves the divine hypothesis relative to alternatives rather than demanding their complete exclusion. Locked score: The mixed band reflects relevant pressure on skeptical methodology but only partial responsiveness, unstable evidential terminology, materially overstated impossibility, and insufficient charity toward the stated concession.

pro-unspecified-alternative-not-defeater.words: A merely unspecified possible explanation does not defeat an abductive case unless a substantive competing account or a concrete objection to the offered comparison is supplied.
pro-unspecified-alternative-not-defeater.critique: Strongest feature: The move correctly distinguishes a bare logical possibility from a developed defeater, protecting ordinary abductive reasoning from paralysis whenever someone can merely imagine that an unidentified alternative might exist. Principal limitation: Candidate-set incompleteness can rationally lower confidence without furnishing a complete rival, especially when priors, selection effects, causal baselines, or the hypothesis space are materially unconstrained, and the response leaves those actual comparative-data objections unanswered. Live burden: The pro side must establish the initial case's strength, specify when unknown alternatives become negligible, and compare live impersonal or naturalistic accounts rather than requiring opponents to deliver a fully formed replacement. Locked score: The strong band reflects a plausible and relevant subsidiary principle with good logical coherence, moderated by partial responsiveness, slightly overstated force, and inadequate engagement with the strongest underdetermination argument.

pro-function-does-not-answer-grounding.words: Agreement that transcendental facts operate reliably does not answer the distinct meta-level question of what explains or grounds the facts themselves.
pro-function-does-not-answer-grounding.critique: Strongest feature: The reply precisely distinguishes object-level agreement about the operation of transcendental facts from the meta-level request for their explanation, directly diagnosing why a purely functional description may leave the original grounding question untouched. Principal limitation: Identifying an unanswered question does not independently establish that a further ontological ground is required, much less that the appropriate ground is personal, necessary, or divine, so the positive inference remains outside this successful distinction. Live burden: The pro side must justify the explanatory demand and show that a descriptive or fundamental account is incomplete rather than merely restating the request at another level. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional clarity, matched calibration, charitable representation, and complete contact with the immediate reply, while preserving the limited but important qualification that raising the meta-question does not answer it.

pro-cumulative-public-revelation.words: Creation, morality, transcendental facts, special revelation, Jesus, and the resurrection collectively form publicly available evidence against the claim that God remains hidden.
pro-cumulative-public-revelation.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly denies hiddenness by presenting a cumulative and publicly oriented set of alleged disclosures across natural, moral, transcendental, historical, and revelatory domains rather than relying on private experience alone. Principal limitation: Listing evidential categories does not establish their reliability, independence, clarity, or discrimination, and describing the totality as sufficient for any reasonable person understates persistent informed disagreement and alternative explanations. Live burden: The cumulative case must assess dependence among components, support its historical and theological premises, compare religiously plural interpretations, and explain why reasonable nonbelief persists despite supposedly adequate disclosure. Locked score: The strong band reflects direct responsiveness, broad explanatory scope, and a recognizable cumulative strategy, tempered by materially overstated force, compressed public-warrant claims, limited evidence for the listed components, and incomplete engagement with the strongest ambiguity objection.

con-unfulfilled-divine-disclosure-aim.words: If God desires universal knowledge and possesses an effective means to secure it, persistent nonbelief counts against attributing that unfulfilled intention to God.
con-unfulfilled-divine-disclosure-aim.critique: Strongest feature: The reply formulates a tightly conditional test linking an asserted universal divine desire, an effective disclosure mechanism, and the observed failure to achieve universal knowledge, thereby making its evidential consequence transparent and proportionate. Principal limitation: The argument does not independently establish that universal actual knowledge is the relevant divine aim or that the proposed mechanism guarantees uptake, and its force diminishes if revelation instead seeks adequate opportunity, responsibility, or noncompelled relationship. Live burden: The skeptical side must ground the attributed intention in the pro position, distinguish knowledge from compelled conviction, and show that reasonable nonbelief conflicts with the narrower disclosure aim actually defended. Locked score: The very strong band reflects explicit qualification, excellent logical coherence, strong responsiveness, and charitable confinement of the inference, with the remaining limitation located in its conditional antecedents rather than its internal structure.

pro-revelation-obligation-not-compulsion.words: God may reveal enough to impose an obligation to know without intending to compel every person to acquire settled conviction or actual belief.
pro-revelation-obligation-not-compulsion.critique: Strongest feature: The reply precisely corrects the attributed divine aim by distinguishing universal revelation and obligation from universal settled knowledge, conviction, or compelled belief, thereby defeating the opponent's conditional in the form immediately presented. Principal limitation: Reframing the aim does not establish that the alleged revelation is sufficiently clear or accessible to create the claimed obligation, and persistent reasonable nonbelief may still challenge adequate universal opportunity without implying literal compulsion. Live burden: The pro side must explain the epistemic threshold for obligation, demonstrate that creation and other disclosures meet it across diverse circumstances, and address sincere nonbelief under the narrower formulation. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional precision, proportionate calibration, justified reframing, and decisive responsiveness, while retaining a substantive downstream question about whether the available evidence actually grounds the obligation asserted.

strengths: Clearly separated the operation of transcendental facts from the further meta-level grounding question.
Presented a unified explanatory framework using coherence, scope, power, parsimony, and low ad hocness.
Correctly defended philosophical and abductive reasoning as potentially legitimate evidence rather than requiring laboratory repetition.
Precisely distinguished revelation sufficient for obligation from an intention to compel universal settled belief.

blunders.text: The central move from logical attributes to a personal mind did not exhaust impersonal alternatives or establish that abstract truth must be mental.
The necessary-ground argument gave God explanatory termination without adequately showing why necessary logical facts could not be similarly fundamental.

tags.label: Special pleading
tags.context: The exception for divine necessity lacked a developed principle unavailable to necessary logical facts.

blunders.text: The cumulative revelation case listed evidence categories without establishing their independence, reliability, or power to resolve reasonable disagreement.

strengths: Required evidence to discriminate reliably in favor of a sufficiently specific hypothesis.
Exposed the incomplete candidate set and missing comparative likelihood information in the divine abduction.
Distinguished evidence toward generic agency from confirmation of Yahweh or a necessary personal deity.
Offered a clear descriptive alternative on which logical relations need no additional guaranteeing entity.
Kept the disclosure objection explicitly conditional on a universal divine aim and effective mechanism.

blunders.text: The hiddenness argument did not answer the immediate inference from logical attributes to a personal ground and left divine aims underspecified.
The candidate-set objection sometimes suggested a near-exhaustive comparison was needed without defining a workable threshold for responsible abduction.
The broader suggestion that good supernatural evidence might be unavailable exceeded the narrower comparative-data objection supported in the exchange.

newArguments.title: Normative unity argument
newArguments.text: Logical truths do more than describe which inferences people happen to make: they distinguish reasoning that should be accepted from reasoning that should be rejected. A necessary rational ground could explain why modal truth, inferential normativity, and rational intelligibility belong to one structure. This does not follow merely from calling logic abstract, and it does not establish a specific religion. It offers a new comparative question: whether impersonal accounts explain normative authority and rational accessibility together as economically as a necessary rational source does.

novelty.explanation: This is a genuinely new line based on the joint explanatory target of normativity, modality, and accessibility.

newArguments.title: Prediction through cognitive fit
newArguments.text: A personal-ground hypothesis can be made more discriminating by deriving a modest expectation: finite rational creatures in an ordered world should possess broadly reliable access to basic logical relations, while retaining fallibility because their cognition is limited. The relevant datum is not simply that logic exists, but that abstract reasoning successfully coordinates inquiry across mathematics, language, and empirical science. This prediction needs comparison with evolutionary and structuralist accounts, yet it gives the hypothesis more content than a vague appeal to an unspecified creator.

novelty.explanation: This answers the vagueness challenge by supplying a defeasible prediction and an explicit comparative requirement.

thesis.text: Transcendental facts do not presently constitute good evidence for a necessary personal God because the divine hypothesis lacks sufficiently distinctive predictions and demonstrated comparative advantage over impersonal accounts.

novelty.explanation: This consolidates the strongest skeptical moves into a precise comparative thesis without denying all philosophical evidence.

premises.text: Evidence favors a hypothesis when the observed facts are more expected under that hypothesis than under relevant competitors, not merely when the hypothesis is compatible with them.

novelty.explanation: This formalizes the transcript's reliable-discrimination standard as comparative evidential support.

premises.text: Necessary logical relations are compatible with several families of views, including impersonal realism, structuralism, conceptualism, naturalized accounts, and positions treating such relations as fundamental.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's independence and descriptive alternatives into an explicit competitor set.

premises.text: The generic necessary-mind hypothesis does not yet specify what logical structure, cognitive accessibility, religious disclosure, or world history should be expected rather than merely permitted.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the vague hiddenness appeal by identifying concrete predictive dimensions that require specification.

premises.text: Without comparative likelihoods or independent evidence of divine mentality, moving from explanatory dissatisfaction with impersonal views to a personal ground risks substituting a label for an explanation.

novelty.explanation: This combines the comparative-data and premise-support objections while preserving a defeasible evidential standard.

conclusion.text: Therefore, withholding assent to the personal-God inference is warranted unless a more specific divine model generates distinctive expectations and demonstrably compares better with serious impersonal alternatives.

novelty.explanation: This gives the skeptical case a proportionate conclusion of withholding rather than asserting that no divine evidence is possible.

newArguments.title: Model multiplicity argument
newArguments.text: A grounding explanation should reduce uncertainty, but adding a necessary mind may multiply unresolved models: Does logic constitute that mind's nature, arise from its thoughts, or constrain it independently? Each option carries different consequences for necessity, arbitrariness, and explanatory priority. Until the theistic account selects and defends one model, apparent unity may conceal several incompatible explanations. This is not an appeal to an unknown alternative; it is an internal model-selection problem showing that the phrase personal ground does not yet determine how the proposed explanation works.

novelty.explanation: This genuinely new argument identifies unresolved internal variants within the divine-ground hypothesis itself.

newArguments.title: Common-data symmetry
newArguments.text: Both theism and impersonal realism begin with the same data: logical necessity, objective validity, and human access to basic inference. If each view can accommodate those facts, the evidence discriminates only when one predicts them with fewer auxiliary assumptions or independently supported mechanisms. Theistic language about rationality may make the fit feel intuitive, but intuition is not yet a likelihood comparison. The skeptical case can therefore grant the full transcendental data while asking for an asymmetry that favors personality rather than merely restating the data in personal terms.

novelty.explanation: This strengthens the discrimination objection by defining the specific evidential asymmetry the theistic case must establish.
